issues.description: Method getNumberOfStudentsPerTutor(): the problem statement's UML declares getNumberOfStudentsPerTutor() returns a double, but the solution implements getNumberOfStudentsPerTutor() as an int. The template contains only a TODO for this method (no signature). This mismatch between the UML and the solution implementation is confusing for students: the UML suggests a floating-point result (allowing fractional students-per-tutor), while the solution uses integer division and returns an int. Students may implement the method with the wrong return type or be unsure whether fractional values are expected.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the return type consistent across artifacts. Preferred fix: change the solution (and update the template signature hint) so getNumberOfStudentsPerTutor() returns a double and computes the value with floating-point division, e.g. public double getNumberOfStudentsPerTutor() { return (double) getTotalNumberOfStudents() / getNumberOfTutors(); }. Alternatively, if integer division is intended, update the UML and problem text to specify an int return type and clarify that fractional students-per-tutor are rounded/truncated.
